faith.omen.runes.voyage.ill: The seer frowns at the runes and will not meet your eye. By evening the crews mutter that Saltha is hungry this season.
faith.omen.runes.voyage.uncertain: The runes fall crosswise. The seer shrugs: the sea will be the sea.
faith.omen.runes.voyage.fair: The seer nods over the runes. The steersmen say the Mother of the Sea will be gentle enough.
faith.omen.runes.voyage.blessed: The seer smiles at the runes, and word runs along the strand that Saltha and the Wanderer favour this voyage. The men are eager for the oars.
faith.omen.runes.battle.ill: The seer turns one rune face down and says nothing. By nightfall the hird whispers of ill luck in the coming fight.
faith.omen.runes.battle.uncertain: “Spears break on both sides,” says the seer, and no more.
faith.omen.runes.battle.fair: The seer reads strength in the runes. The warriors bang their shields: Dunnar stands with the folk.
faith.omen.runes.battle.blessed: Ravens circled the hall at dawn, and the seer’s runes agree. The hird believes it cannot lose.
faith.omen.runes.duel.ill: The seer’s hand hesitates over the oath-rune. Your champions grow quiet.
faith.omen.runes.duel.uncertain: The oath-rune lies on its side. The seer will promise nothing.
faith.omen.runes.duel.fair: The seer marks the oath-rune with a nod. Men say the law is with your cause.
faith.omen.runes.duel.blessed: The oath-rune falls upright between Dunnar’s and Eidr’s. Whoever stands in the square for you walks taller.
faith.omen.runes.harvest.ill: The seer crumbles a dry ear of barley and sighs. The farmers fear a lean year.
faith.omen.runes.harvest.uncertain: The seer speaks of rain and of sun, and of neither too much.
faith.omen.runes.harvest.fair: The seer smiles over the barley-rune. The farmers say Fjorna’s tears will fall in good measure.
faith.omen.runes.harvest.blessed: The seer laughs aloud at the runes. In the steadings they are already brewing for the harvest feast.
faith.omen.signs.voyage.ill: The priest watches the gulls fly inland and makes the sign of the Flame. The crews take it badly.
faith.omen.signs.voyage.uncertain: The priest prays over the ships and will say only that the sea belongs to the One Flame.
faith.omen.signs.voyage.fair: The altar candle burns tall and still. The priest blesses the hulls, and the crews row easier for it.
faith.omen.signs.voyage.blessed: A clear dawn over the harbour, which the priest names a sign of grace. The crews believe him and pull hard.
faith.omen.signs.battle.ill: The altar flame gutters while the priest prays for victory. The warriors exchange looks.
faith.omen.signs.battle.uncertain: The priest prays for a just outcome, which is not the same as a victory.
faith.omen.signs.battle.fair: The priest blesses the spears and the banner. The men stand straighter.
faith.omen.signs.battle.blessed: The priest proclaims the steady candle a sign. The warriors believe the One Flame marches with them.
faith.omen.signs.duel.ill: The priest prays for your champion with a worried face.
faith.omen.signs.duel.uncertain: “Let the just cause prevail,” says the priest, and leaves it there.
faith.omen.signs.duel.fair: The priest blesses your champion’s blade. Men say heaven sees the right of it.
faith.omen.signs.duel.blessed: The priest calls the signs plain: right is on your side. Your champion believes him.
faith.omen.signs.harvest.ill: The priest leads the procession around the fields under a grey sky. The farmers fear a lean year.
faith.omen.signs.harvest.uncertain: The priest blesses the seed and promises nothing.
faith.omen.signs.harvest.fair: The priest blesses the fields, and the farmers go home content.
faith.omen.signs.harvest.blessed: The fields are blessed under a bright sky; the farmers call it a sign of plenty and work with a will.
faith.omen.read: {signs, select, lantern {The priests have read the signs} other {The seer has cast the runes}}: voyage {voyage, select, ill {Ill} uncertain {Uncertain} fair {Fair} blessed {Blessed} other {unread}}, battle {battle, select, ill {Ill} uncertain {Uncertain} fair {Fair} blessed {Blessed} other {unread}}, duel {duel, select, ill {Ill} uncertain {Uncertain} fair {Fair} blessed {Blessed} other {unread}}, harvest {harvest, select, ill {Ill} uncertain {Uncertain} fair {Fair} blessed {Blessed} other {unread}}.
faith.omen.tooltip: An omen is what your people believe about the coming venture. Confident crews row harder and wait for the right weather; worried ones grumble and hurry.
faith.sacrifice.done: The offering to {god, select, valgrim {Valgrim} dunnar {Dunnar} saltha {Saltha} fjorna {Fjorna} eidr {Eidr} skell {Skell} grayQueen {the Gray Queen} other {the gods}} is made at the grove of {settlement}. Your people take heart. (Favor +{gain})
faith.sacrifice.unheeded: The offering to {god, select, valgrim {Valgrim} dunnar {Dunnar} saltha {Saltha} fjorna {Fjorna} eidr {Eidr} skell {Skell} grayQueen {the Gray Queen} other {the gods}} is made, but the seer says the god has had enough from your house this month. (no Favor gained)
faith.sacrifice.narration.silver: Silver rings into the sacred pool, and the seer calls out the name of {god, select, valgrim {Valgrim} dunnar {Dunnar} saltha {Saltha} fjorna {Fjorna} eidr {Eidr} skell {Skell} grayQueen {the Gray Queen} other {the gods}}.
faith.sacrifice.narration.livestock: The beasts are led into the grove for {god, select, valgrim {Valgrim} dunnar {Dunnar} saltha {Saltha} fjorna {Fjorna} eidr {Eidr} skell {Skell} grayQueen {the Gray Queen} other {the gods}}. Blood is sprinkled on the posts, and the meat is boiled for the feast that follows.
faith.sacrifice.narration.unheeded: “Enough,” says the seer, taking the offering without ceremony. “Even gods tire of the same faces.”
faith.alms.done: Alms are given at {settlement}. The poor bless your name. (Piety +{piety})
faith.deed.battleWon: {signs, select, lantern {The priests give thanks for the victory. (Piety +{piety})} other {The hird says the Wanderer’s ravens fed well today, and men believe Valgrim watched the fight. (Valgrim +{amount})}}
faith.deed.seaBattleWon: {signs, select, lantern {The priests give thanks for the victory at sea. (Piety +{piety})} other {The sailors pour a cup into the sea for Saltha and boast that the Wanderer steered their arrows. (Valgrim and Saltha +{amount})}}
faith.deed.holdingDefended: {signs, select, lantern {The folk you defended light candles for your house in the chapel. (Piety +{piety})} other {The folk you defended carve Dunnar’s hammer on their doorposts. They say Stormfist stands with your house. (Dunnar +{amount})}}
faith.deed.feastHeld: {signs, select, lantern {The feast opens with a blessing, and the priests are pleased. (Piety +{piety})} other {The feast is loud and long, and the folk drink to Dunnar’s health and yours. (Dunnar +{amount})}}
faith.deed.harvestFeast: {signs, select, lantern {The harvest is blessed at the altar before the feast. (Piety +{piety})} other {The harvest feast honours Fjorna Goldtear; the farmers say she will remember it. (Fjorna +{amount})}}
faith.deed.marriage: {signs, select, lantern {The marriage is blessed before the altar. (Piety +{piety})} other {The women wreathe the bride’s hair, and everyone agrees that Goldtear smiles on the match. (Fjorna +{amount})}}
faith.deed.giftGiven: {signs, select, lantern {The priests praise your generosity. (Piety +{piety})} other {Open-handedness is Fjorna’s way; the gift is talked about in every hall. (Fjorna +{amount})}}
faith.deed.stormSurvived: The crews came through the storm and swear Saltha let them go. They pour ale over the side in thanks. (Saltha +{amount})
faith.deed.holmgangWon: Your champion walks out of the holmgang square alive. Men say Eidr the Oath-Bound judged the quarrel. (Eidr +{amount})
faith.deed.duelWon: The duel is won. Men say Eidr favours those who stand behind their words. (Eidr +{amount})
faith.deed.oathKept: {signs, select, lantern {The priests note that your house keeps its word. (Piety +{piety})} other {Men note that your house keeps its word, as Eidr demands. (Eidr +{amount})}}
faith.deed.oathBroken: {signs, select, lantern {An oath is broken, and the priests preach on faithlessness. (Piety {piety, number})} other {An oath is broken. The lawspeakers mutter that Eidr will not forget. (Eidr {amount, number})}}
faith.deed.weregildPaid: {signs, select, lantern {The weregild is paid; the priests call it a righteous act. (Piety +{piety})} other {The weregild is paid in full before witnesses. The law is satisfied, and so, men say, is Eidr. (Eidr +{amount})}}
faith.deed.hallBurned: {signs, select, lantern {The priests are troubled by the burning. (Piety {piety, number})} other {The flames are seen for miles. Skell’s sworn men laugh and say the Laughing Flame danced tonight. (Skell +{amount})}}
faith.deed.foeTricked: The ruse worked. Those who swear by Skell say the outcast god loves a clever trick. (Skell +{amount})
faith.deed.properFuneral: {signs, select, lantern {The dead are buried with prayers and candles. (Piety +{piety})} other {The dead are sent off with grave-goods and ale, as the old customs ask. The household says the Gray Queen is content. (the Gray Queen +{amount})}}
faith.deed.famineEndured: The hungry months are behind you. The old women say the Gray Queen spared the household. (the Gray Queen +{amount})
faith.deed.legendLearned: A new tale for the hall. The seers say Valgrim rewards those who seek wisdom. (Valgrim +{amount})
faith.deed.relicFound: {signs, select, lantern {The relic is shown in the chapel, and pilgrims begin to talk of it. (Piety +{piety})} other {The relic is carried home in triumph. The faithful say {god, select, valgrim {Valgrim} dunnar {Dunnar} saltha {Saltha} fjorna {Fjorna} eidr {Eidr} skell {Skell} grayQueen {the Gray Queen} other {the gods}} has shown favour. (Favor +{amount})}}
faith.deed.templeSteadRaided: Blood on a temple-stead. Even your own warriors are uneasy, and men say the gods will remember. (every god {amount, number})
faith.deed.groveDesecrated: A sacred grove is defiled. Your people are frightened of what the gods will do. (every god {amount, number})
faith.deed.missionaryWelcomed: The old families grumble that welcoming the Lantern’s priests insults the gods of your fathers. (every god {amount, number})
faith.deed.missionarySentAway: The Lantern’s missionaries are sent on their way. The seers and the old families approve. (every god +{amount})
faith.deed.pilgrimage: The pilgrimage is made and talked about across the Lantern lands. (Piety +{piety})
faith.wrath.raised: Word of what was done at {settlement} spreads through the Lantern lands. (Faith Wrath +{amount})
faith.wrath.rose.sermons: Priests across the Lantern realms preach against your house, and their kings listen. (Faith Wrath {value}: opinion {opinion, number} with every Lantern realm)
faith.wrath.rose.muster: The Lantern’s bishops call for a muster against your house. Men say a war fleet is gathering in the south. (Faith Wrath {value})
faith.wrath.rose.ban: The Ban of the Flame is proclaimed: no Lantern market will trade with your house. (Faith Wrath {value})
faith.wrath.fell.sermons: The sermons against your house grow quieter. (Faith Wrath {value})
faith.wrath.fell.muster: The call to muster against your house loses its fire. (Faith Wrath {value})
faith.wrath.fell.ban: The Ban of the Flame is quietly allowed to lapse. (Faith Wrath {value})
faith.chronicle.wrath.sermons: Priests of the Lantern preached against the house.
faith.chronicle.wrath.muster: The Lantern called a muster against the house.
faith.chronicle.wrath.ban: The Ban of the Flame was proclaimed against the house.
faith.chapel.built: A chapel of the Lantern now stands in {settlement}.
faith.conversion.done: Your house has taken the Lantern. The priests rejoice; the old families do not. The Lantern realms think better of you, and the church forgives past wrongs.
faith.conversion.holding: Most of the folk of {settlement} now keep the Lantern.
faith.chronicle.conversion: The house turned from the old gods and took the Lantern.
faith.error.noRuler: Your house has no living ruler.
faith.error.notAtSettlement: Your ruler must be at a settlement.
faith.error.notEnoughSilver: You do not have enough silver.
faith.error.notEnoughLivestock: The holding’s herds and stores are too thin for this offering.
faith.error.wrongFaith: Your house does not keep that faith.
faith.error.noGrove: Offerings are made at a grove in one of your holdings, or at a temple-stead.
faith.error.hostile: You are at war with this place.
faith.error.noPriest: There is no church or chapel here.
faith.error.seerCooldown: The seer will not cast the runes again so soon. Come back next month.
faith.error.alreadyConverted: Your house already keeps the Lantern.
faith.error.noChapel: There must first be a chapel in one of your holdings.
faith.error.lanternOpinionTooLow: The Lantern realms do not yet think well enough of your house.
faith.error.notYourHolding: Chapels are founded in your own holdings.
faith.error.chapelExists: This holding already has a chapel.
faith.ui.seer.lede: Ask the rune-seer what the coming season holds, and have the wounded tended.
faith.ui.seer.omensDesc: The seer casts the runes for voyages, battles, duels and the harvest. What your people believe steadies them or unsettles them.
faith.ui.seer.readyOn: The seer will cast again on {date}
faith.ui.seer.cooldown: A seer casts for your house once every {days} days.
faith.ui.seer.noReadings: No reading is in force. Until the runes are cast, every venture is uncertain.
faith.ui.seer.later: Legends, relic clues and readings of a child’s fate are not yet told here.
faith.ui.effect.moralePct: Warriors fight with {sign}{value}% heart in battle
faith.ui.heal.title: Tending the wounded
faith.ui.heal.desc: Rest heals in time. A seer of your house (or a church, for houses near one) shortens the mending, and only a skilled seer can save a mortal wound.
faith.ui.heal.none: No one of your house is wounded.
faith.ui.heal.treated: Already tended. Rest will do the rest.
faith.ui.grove.lede: Make offerings to the gods. Favor feeds the omens and the gods’ own gifts.
faith.ui.grove.away: Your ruler is away from any grove
faith.ui.grove.notOldWays: Your house keeps {faith}. Groves are for the Old Ways.
faith.ui.grove.offeredThisMonth: {count, plural, one {One offering this month} other {# offerings this month}}
faith.ui.grove.diminished: The god has had enough from your house this month: this offering would bring no Favor.
faith.ui.grove.rules: Each further offering to the same god in one month brings less Favor. Livestock counts for more than silver; a greater grove multiplies the gain.
faith.ui.grove.about: Favor runs from {min} to {max} for each god. A god left untended loses {neglect} Favor each month.
faith.ui.godEffect.valgrim: The seer casts one extra rune for every {perDie} Favor, making the readings surer.
faith.ui.godEffect.dunnar: His Favor steadies your warriors in battles and duels through the omens.
faith.ui.godEffect.saltha: Her Favor calms the sea in the voyage omens.
faith.ui.godEffect.fjorna: Children come more readily to a house in her Favor ({pct}% likelier for each point of Favor).
faith.ui.godEffect.eidr: His Favor stiffens your champion’s nerve through the duel omens.
faith.ui.godEffect.skell: The outcast god feeds no reading; his Favor is a matter of reputation.
faith.ui.godEffect.grayQueen: At {min} Favor or more, your house’s old folk die a little less often of age.
faith.ui.seer.scene: Smoke hangs under the low roof. The seer waits by the fire with the rune-bag.
faith.ui.seer.choices: What do you ask of the seer?
faith.ui.seer.readLine: {cost} silver. The seer casts once every {days} days.
faith.ui.seer.healLine: {count, plural, =0 {No one of your house is hurt.} one {One of your house is hurt.} other {# of your house are hurt.}}
faith.ui.heal.noHealer: No seer of your house is here to tend them. Appoint one in the Longhouse.
faith.ui.grove.scene: Old trees, a carved post and the ash of the last fire. The gods listen here.
